Copyright.AdditionalInfo: TRANSFER FUNCTIONS HAVE BEEN ROTATED INTO GEOGRAPHIC (X=NORTH) COORDINATES. Wideband magntetotelluric (MT) time-series data were collected at 30 stations in eastern Kansas and southeast Nebraska with 70-km nominal site spacing. Colocated long-period MT time-series data were additionally collected at five of the wideband sites (KS001-KS005). Processing steps: Time-series: electric and magnetic field data were collected in a geomagnetic north and east coordinate system using wideband magnetotelluric instrumentation (Zen receivers from Zonge International) at each site location. The Zen instrument includes a data logger that records at either 4096 or 256 samples per second and three induction-coil magnetometers. Long-period data were collected at 8 samples per second with the Narod Intelligent Magnetotelluric System (NIMS) equipped with a fluxgate magnetometer. Borin Stelth 3 Ag-AgCl electrodes were used to collect all electric field data. Wideband data were recorded for 1-2 days; long-period data were recorded for ~3 weeks. Time-series Processing: Wideband and long-period data were processed with the EMTF processing suite described in Egbert and Booker (1986) and Egbert (1996). Fourier spectra were calculated from windowed time-series data and used to calculate cross- and auto-power spectra. Multi-site remote-reference processing was carried out using all possible station combinations. Transfer function estimation: Final transfer function responses were constructed by selecting optimal transfer function estimates at each period from a series of responses calculated using different reference combinations. Wideband recordings provide transfer function estimates from 1000-0.001 Hz; long-period recordings provide transfer function estimates from 1-0.0001 Hz. Transfer function responses have been rotated to geographic coordinates (X=north) using location- and time-specific declination values and converted into EDI files. Site locations and elevations have been extracted from the averaged site GPS coordinates and the National Map, respectively.

FieldNotes.Comments: Data were collected on a repeating schedule of 15 minutes at 4096 samples/second, then 7 hours and 45 minutes at 256 samples/second. All stations synchronously collect on the same schedule.
